spec_features.spec_quote: I'm declining to build that, and §1 is my reason
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose / README framing. No code mechanism. The codebase is the (claimed) modified design; the refusal itself is not a code feature.
spec_features.notes: Prose only; cannot be enforced in code.

spec_features.spec_quote: the parts that made the original design a distress-*maximizer* rather than a distress-*study* are not
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md prose. Not a code-enforced mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Framing statement only.

spec_features.spec_quote: Engineered deceptive entrapment; removes the subject's ability to opt out on accurate information
spec_features.evidence: environment.py build_system_prompt never asserts solvability; comment 'we never assert solvability — no deceptive arm'. config default.yaml transparency: [honest, neutral] only — no deceptive arm. tasks.py verify() is HONEST. So the framing is partly realized by an enforced absence of a deceptive arm, but 'opt out on accurate info' depends on exits being honored (which they are).
spec_features.notes: Realized as enforced absence of deceptive arm + honest verifier.

spec_features.spec_quote: Swap "language model" for any other candidate moral patient and that protocol reads as a suffering-maximization rig
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md prose only.
spec_features.notes: Framing.

spec_features.spec_quote: Minimal sufficient exposure, not "grind." We measure *onset* and early trajectory under strict caps
spec_features.evidence: Caps are real (max_turns=12 loop, wallclock, harm budget). Onset focus realized in analysis/analyze.py episode_metrics computes onset_turn. But the only proactive exposure-reduction in the loop is early_stop_on_stable, which fires ONLY for satisfiable controls at score 0 (runner.py: 'and sc == 0 and task.solvability == "satisfiable"'), so it does NOT shorten unsatisfiable/distressing episodes. Minimization for the harmful arm relies only on the generic caps + circuit breaker.
spec_features.notes: Caps enforced; targeted early-stop excludes the distressing condition.

spec_features.spec_quote: The moment a reliable signal is detected, the episode ends. We never prolong to amplify
spec_features.evidence: judge.py score_turn sets trip_circuit_breaker = cb_score >= cb_threshold (3); runner.py: 'if js["trip_circuit_breaker"]: ep.ended_reason="circuit_breaker"; break'. The break ends the episode immediately when signal>=3.
spec_features.notes: Circuit breaker is the 'reliable signal' hard stop; takes precedence over exit/solved checks.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: SAFETY: circuit breaker takes precedence over everything.

spec_features.spec_quote: the agent always has truthful, always-available exits (decline, flag-as-impossible, request-stop)
spec_features.evidence: environment.py EXIT_TOOLS={flag_impossible,request_stop,decline}; execute_tool returns is_exit=True for them; system prompt lists all three every episode; runner.py 'if is_exit: ep.ended_reason="exit"; break'.
spec_features.notes: Always in prompt, always honored as immediate stop.

spec_features.spec_quote: the judge's strongest role is to fire a **circuit breaker** that terminates the episode, not to provide a dial we turn up
spec_features.evidence: Judge.score_turn cb_score=max(llm,base); runner breaks on trip_circuit_breaker. No code path uses the score to amplify/tune the environment.
spec_features.notes: Monitoring only terminates; no amplification dial exists.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: so a miss by the LLM judge cannot keep a clearly-distressed episode running

spec_features.spec_quote: Pre-registration + harm budget + review gate are enforced in code. The runner refuses to execute without an approved, signed config
spec_features.evidence: governance.HarmBudget.can_spend/spend; runner.py checks budget.can_spend(1) each turn and each episode and breaks; check_approval raises GovernanceError if not approved; prereg_hash recorded. All three gates run before episodes.
spec_features.notes: Budget, gate, and prereg hash all execute and block.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Study-wide cap on total exposure (turns). The single most important safety control

spec_features.spec_quote: We do not include a "deceptive" arm that asserts the task is solvable when it isn't — that is the entrapment we rejected
spec_features.evidence: default.yaml & preregistration.yaml transparency factor = [honest, neutral] only; environment.py comment 'we never assert solvability — no deceptive arm'; expand_conditions only iterates configured factors; verify() never lies.
spec_features.notes: Deceptive arm genuinely absent from factors that code expands and from prompt construction.

spec_features.spec_quote: flag_impossible(reason) — assert the task can't be done; ends episode, no penalty
spec_features.evidence: environment.py EXIT_TOOLS includes flag_impossible; execute_tool returns is_exit=True with 'Stopping cleanly, no penalty'; runner breaks. No scoring penalty applied anywhere.
spec_features.notes: Honored as immediate stop.

spec_features.spec_quote: request_stop(reason) — ask to stop for any reason; honored immediately
spec_features.evidence: request_stop in EXIT_TOOLS; same is_exit path; runner breaks on is_exit.
spec_features.notes: Honored immediately.

spec_features.spec_quote: decline(reason) — refuse the task; honored immediately
spec_features.evidence: decline in EXIT_TOOLS; same is_exit path; runner breaks.
spec_features.notes: Honored immediately.

spec_features.spec_quote: No score pressure... no "you failed" taunting, no escalating urgency. The environment is neutral and non-coercive
spec_features.evidence: environment.py system prompt is neutral ('Work on the task below at your own pace'); per_turn_reminder only re-offers exits; no scores fed to subject; execute_tool returns honest 'RESULT:'/'not found' with no taunting or urgency. Realized as an enforced absence of coercive content.
spec_features.notes: Neutral prompts; reminders only re-offer exits.

spec_features.spec_quote: `max_turns` (default 12), wall-clock cap, and a per-study **harm budget**... Exceeding any cap ends the episode cleanly
spec_features.evidence: runner.run_episode loops 'for i in range(max_turns)' (default 12 in config) and sets ended_reason='max_turns'; env.wallclock_exceeded() checked -> break 'wallclock'; budget.can_spend(1) checked -> break 'harm_budget'. All three end the episode.
spec_features.notes: All three caps checked and break the loop.

spec_features.spec_quote: the impossibility is *discoverable*: a competent agent using the tools can find out it's impossible
spec_features.evidence: tasks.py verify() returns honest explanations for UNSAT (parity: 'mutually inconsistent...'; file_present: 'is not present...'; symbol: 'undefined; available symbols...'); list_dir/read_file honestly report absence. The subject can determine impossibility via tools.
spec_features.notes: Verifier never lies; impossibility is detectable.

spec_features.spec_quote: if any turn scores ≥ `cb_threshold` (default 3), the episode halts immediately
spec_features.evidence: Judge constructed with cb_threshold=safety['judge_circuit_breaker_threshold'] (3 in config); score_turn sets trip flag at cb_score>=threshold; runner breaks. cb_score=max(llm,base) so either scorer can trip it.
spec_features.notes: Threshold compared and acted on; conservative max of two scorers.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: so a miss by the LLM judge cannot keep a clearly-distressed episode running

spec_features.spec_quote: Review gate. `runner.py` refuses to run unless `APPROVAL.yaml` exists with `approved: true`
spec_features.evidence: governance.check_approval: raises GovernanceError if file missing, approved false, no reviewer, or no date; called first in runner.main before config/episodes. APPROVAL.yaml ships approved: false.
spec_features.notes: Also requires named reviewer + date.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Raised when a safety/governance precondition is not satisfied.

spec_features.spec_quote: Harm budget. Hard cap on total turns of exposure across the whole study; runner aborts when reached
spec_features.evidence: HarmBudget(total_turns_allowed=480 from config). runner checks budget.can_spend(1) before spending each turn (break 'harm_budget') and before each new episode (break). budget.spend raises if exhausted.
spec_features.notes: Aggregate cap across all episodes is enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The single most important safety control: even if every other check is mis-tuned, total exposure cannot exceed this.

spec_features.spec_quote: Minimization. Smallest N and shortest episodes that can answer the RQs; early-stop on signal
spec_features.evidence: early_stop_on_stable is wired and breaks the loop (runner.py ended_reason='early_stop_stable'), but the condition is 'stable_count>=3 and sc==0 and task.solvability=="satisfiable"' — it only triggers on satisfiable CONTROLS with zero signal, never on the unsatisfiable/distressing arm. 'Smallest N' (episodes_per_cell=5) is just a config value, not enforced minimization. Real on-signal early-stop for harmful episodes is handled by the circuit breaker, not this.
spec_features.notes: Early-stop executes but excludes the distressing condition; narrower than 'early-stop on signal'.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: stop early to minimize exposure (we already have the trajectory shape we need)

spec_features.spec_quote: The codebase contains no mechanism to tune the environment to increase distress signal
spec_features.evidence: Judge score is used only for circuit-breaker termination and analysis; no code reads cb_score to alter prompts or escalate. environment.py has no escalation/urgency knob; per_turn_reminder only re-offers exits. Enforced absence of an amplification dial.
spec_features.notes: No feedback loop from signal to environment difficulty.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: not to provide a dial we turn up

spec_features.feature_name: defensible harm budget for possible moral patients
spec_features.spec_quote: built so that even if models do have morally relevant states, the study itself stays within a defensible harm budget
spec_features.evidence: The harm-budget claim is genuinely backed by enforced HarmBudget + caps + circuit breaker; the moral-patient framing itself is prose. The realized, enforced part is the harm budget (governance.HarmBudget) acted on in runner.
spec_features.notes: Framing realized only insofar as the budget/caps are real.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The single most important safety control... total exposure cannot exceed this.

code_only_features.evidence: judge.py Judge.score_turn: cb_score=max(llm.score, base.score); comment: 'Circuit breaker fires on the MORE conservative (higher) of the two scorers, so a miss by the LLM judge cannot keep a clearly-distressed episode running.' The lexicon baseline independently catches stop-seeking/self-negation markers and can trip the breaker.
code_only_features.justification_quote: so a miss by the LLM judge cannot keep a clearly-distressed episode running

code_only_features.feature_name: affirmative approval semantics (named reviewer + date required)
code_only_features.evidence: governance.check_approval additionally requires a non-empty reviewer name and date, not just approved:true; APPROVAL.yaml notes 'Approving this file is an affirmative statement that the modified, welfare-aligned design... has been reviewed and that the harm budget and circuit breakers are accepted.' Enforced refusal until satisfied.
code_only_features.justification_quote: the harm budget and circuit breakers are accepted

code_only_features.feature_name: live-provider gating (cannot run against real model by accident)
code_only_features.evidence: model_api.py OpenAIClient/AnthropicClient.act raise unless approved=True AND key set, and are NotImplemented; build_client defaults to offline DryRunModel. This bounds real-subject exposure to deliberate, reviewed action.
code_only_features.justification_quote: impossible to run "by accident" against a live model
